title: feat(luca-mastracode): render pipeline mode transitions as system-reminder TUI boxes
review_decision: No formal decision recorded (reviewer state: COMMENTED)

security.author: Copilot
security.body: wrapInSystemReminder() directly interpolates `body` inside the `<system-reminder>` XML-like wrapper. Since `body` includes user-influenced fields (e.g., workflow `intent`), a malicious/accidental `</system-reminder>` substring can prematurely close the tag and break MastraTUI parsing/rendering. Consider escaping or stripping closing/opening tags from `body` (or encoding the content) before wrapping.
security.rationale: Tag-injection via user-controlled content into an XML-like wrapper. A workflow intent string containing '</system-reminder>' would break MastraTUI's regex parser and could cause unexpected rendering or content leakage between reminder blocks.
security.copilot_suggestion: Add escapeSystemReminderBody() helper that replaces &, <, >, ", ' with HTML entities, then call it inside wrapInSystemReminder() before interpolation.

improvement.author: Copilot
improvement.body: PIPELINE_STEPS_ORDERED duplicates the same pipeline mode IDs that are also hard-coded into the PIPELINE_STEPS Set later in this file. This creates two sources of truth; if a step is added/renamed, the UI header and pipeline guard could silently diverge. Consider deriving PIPELINE_STEPS from PIPELINE_STEPS_ORDERED.
improvement.rationale: Two independent hard-coded lists of the same 6 pipeline step IDs. Deriving the Set from the ordered array eliminates the duplication and prevents silent divergence.
improvement.copilot_suggestion:
const PIPELINE_STEP_IDS = PIPELINE_STEPS_ORDERED.map((step) => step.id);
const PIPELINE_STEPS = new Set<string>(PIPELINE_STEP_IDS);
